rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account also includes divine speech, the Torah's descent, and some Israelites' transformation into despised apes; fuller details of Moses' story are deferred to the commentary on Hud.
rows.anchor: ويمكنك أن تضيف إليها التكليم ونزول التوراة، ومسخ بعضهم قردة خاسئين.

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: An account says Moses pleaded for his seventy companions after the quake; God offered better replacements, but Moses said he recognized them and knew their scent.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال قلت له إن عبد الله بن عجلان قال في مرضه الذي مات فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's analogy is that God replaced Abdullah ibn Ajlan's companions with better ones, as He had done for Moses.
rows.anchor: المراد أن الله بدل له بعبد الله بن عجلان أصحابا هم خير منه كما فعل بموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī calls the report unusual and inconsistent with the Qur'an's apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: والخبر غريب في بابه ولا يوافق ظاهر الكتاب

rows.speaker: القائم
rows.claim: A report argues that human voters may choose a corrupt leader unknowingly; Moses' selection of hypocrites shows that only God, who knows hidden hearts, can choose an Imam.
rows.anchor: عن القائم عليه السلام قال قلت فأخبرني يا مولاي عن العلة التي تمنع القوم من اختيار إمام لأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's Qur'anic citation is a paraphrased composite of the Moses narrative in al-Aʿrāf and al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: الآية فيها منقولة بالمعنى بمعنى أنها ملفقة من آيات القصة في سورتي الأعراف والنساء

rows.speaker: نوف الحميري
rows.claim: Nawf reports that God promised Moses' chosen seventy that the earth would be a mosque and purifier, His tranquility would be in their homes, and all of them could recite the Torah from memory.
rows.anchor: عن نوف الحميري قال لما اختار موسى قومه سبعين رجلا لميقات ربه قال الله لموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about the trial belongs to Moses' speech about the destruction of the seventy; it is unrelated to the calf episode unless Moses repeated it there.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الآية أعني قوله { إن هي إلا فتنتك } من كلامه عليه السلام في قصة هلاك السبعين

rows.speaker: جندب بن عبد الله البجلي
rows.claim: Jundub reports that an Arab prayed for mercy only for himself and Muhammad; the Prophet replied that this restricted God's vast mercy.
rows.anchor: عن جندب بن عبد الله البجلي قال جاء أعرابي فأناخ راحلته ثم عقلها ثم صلى خلف رسول الله

rows.speaker: سلمان عن النبي
rows.claim: A report from Salman quoting the Prophet says God has one hundred mercies, one shared among creatures and ninety-nine reserved until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن سلمان عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Two recensions attributed to Salman describe one mercy sent to earth for compassion among creatures and ninety-nine retained; one is mawqūf, while Ibn Mardawayh's version quotes the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن سلمان موقوفا وابن مردويه عن سلمان قال قال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the mercy teaching is also transmitted through Shiʿi reports from the Imams of the Prophet's household.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى مروي أيضا من طرق الشيعة عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the later report appears to paraphrase the earlier one but corrupts its meaning by saying God removes the earthly mercy from creation on Judgment Day, leaving creation without the mercy needed to subsist.
rows.anchor: وقد أفسد الراوي المعنى بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the formulation that God gathers all one hundred mercies for believers, which does not entail withdrawing mercy from everyone else.
rows.anchor: أن الله يومئذ يجمع المائة للمؤمنين، وجمع المائة لهم واستعمالها فيهم غير انتزاعها عن غيرهم وتخصيصها بهم

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان عن النبي
rows.claim: A report from Hudhayfa quoting the Prophet says God's forgiveness on Judgment Day will be so vast that even Iblis will hope to receive it.
rows.anchor: عن حذيفة بن اليمان عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في حديث والذي نفسي بيده ليغفرن الله يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: The interpretation under discussion identifies the verse's guided and just community as a Jewish nation, and the author says this view is transmitted from Abu Jaʿfar.
rows.anchor: قال وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls the report weak and denies evidence for such a guided Jewish community today; even if it existed, it would no longer be guided after the Mosaic law was abrogated first by Jesus' law and then by Muhammad's.
rows.anchor: الرواية ضعيفة غير مسلمة ولا خبر عن هذه الأمة اليهودية الهادية العادلة اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some who repeat the story add that Muhammad visited the community on the Night Journey, invited them to Islam, and taught them prayer.
rows.anchor: فأضاف إليها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم نزل إليهم ليلة المعراج ودعاهم فآمنوا به وعلمهم الصلاة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil tells of Israelites who fled persecution through a divinely made underground passage to a remote land, where Muhammad and Gabriel visited them during the Night Journey and taught them prayer.
rows.anchor: فعن مقاتل أن مما فضل الله به محمدا صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أنه عاين ليلة المعراج

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī describes a distant community beyond al-Andalus whose people never disobey God, live among extraordinary precious stones and animals, and neither farm nor work.
rows.anchor: وعن الشعبي قال إن لله عبادا من وراء الأندلس كما بيننا وبين الأندلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī dismisses the varied stories about this community as fabricated and refers back to his prior explanation of the verse.
rows.anchor: إلى غير ذلك مما ورد في قصتهم، وهي جميعا مجعولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's covenant concerning God's lordship is among the Qur'an's most subtle in meaning and remarkable in composition.
rows.anchor: وهي من أدق الآيات القرآنية معنى، وأعجبها نظما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Taking” something from another thing implies separation, but its precise sense varies by context; here it means extracting offspring from backs while the source remains whole, then making each child an independent person through successive generations.
rows.anchor: وهو أخذ بعض المادة منها بحيث لا تنقص المادة المأخوذ منها بحسب صورتها ولا تنقلب عن تمامها واستقلالها ثم تكميل الجزء المأخوذ شيئا تاما مستقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “from their backs” specifies this mode of extraction; individuals become distinct from their parents and from one another, each with an independent soul and personal accountability.
rows.anchor: فهذا مفاد قوله { وإذ أخذ ربك من بني آدم من ظهورهم ذريتهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Witnessing people against themselves means showing them the reality of their own selves so they can experientially know it and testify when called upon; the question specifies that they witness God's lordship over them.
rows.anchor: فإشهادهم على أنفسهم هو إراءتهم حقيقة أنفسهم ليتحملوا ما أريد تحملهم من أمرها ثم يؤدوا ما تحملوه إذا سئلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings cannot own or govern their existence independently: they cannot protect themselves from death and suffering, and the cosmic causes on which they depend are themselves governed by an unseen authority.
rows.anchor: ولو ملك نفسه لوقاها مما يكرهه من الموت وسائر آلام الحياة ومصائبها، ولو استقل بتدبير أمره لم يفتقر إلى الخضوع قبال الأسباب الكونية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Need for a Lord who owns and governs human beings is intrinsic to human nature; all people, regardless of knowledge, age, or status, can sense their dependence.
rows.anchor: الحاجة إلى رب - مالك مدبر - حقيقة الإنسان، والفقر مكتوب على نفسه، والضعف مطبوع على ناصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading understands the testimony as worldly recognition of dependence upon God, expressed either by the self's state or by the logical implication of people's acknowledged need.
rows.anchor: فعلى أحد هذين النوعين من القول أعني القول بلسان الحال والقول بالاستلزام يحمل اعترافهم المحكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Between testimony through one's state and testimony by implication, he says the first is closer because testimony should state its object explicitly rather than merely imply it.
rows.anchor: والأول أقرب وأنسب فإنه لا يكتفي في مقام الشهادة إلا بالصريح من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also proposes a third possibility: divine creative speech discloses purposes through existence itself, so the question and answer may have occurred through creation as real speech in an analytical sense.
rows.anchor: فإن الكلام الإلهي يكشف به عن المقاصد الإلهية بالفعل، والإيجاد كلام حقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage says the covenant and testimony were meant to complete God's proof by closing two excuses people might otherwise raise on Judgment Day for their polytheism.
rows.anchor: وهو على ما يفيده السياق إبطال حجتين للعباد على الله وبيان أنه لولا هذا الأخذ والإشهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God had not made anyone testify, all people could plead that they were unaware of His lordship, and an unaware person is not liable to punishment.
rows.anchor: لأقاموا جميعا الحجة علينا يوم القيامة بأنهم كانوا غافلين في الدنيا عن ربوبيتنا، ولا تكليف على غافل ولا مؤاخذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If only the fathers had testified, descendants could plead that they merely imitated their parents without access to the truth; the fathers would be culpable, leaving no complete proof against all humanity.
rows.anchor: وأما الذرية فإنما كان شركهم بمجرد التقليد فيما لا سبيل لهم إلى العلم به لا إجمالا ولا تفصيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If only descendants or some descendants had testified, the others would still be able to plead ignorance; untestified ancestors would neither knowingly shirk nor imitate an earlier example.
rows.anchor: وأما الآباء الذين لم يشهدوا فليس عندهم إلا الغفلة المحضة عن أمر الربوبية فلا يستقلون بشرك إذ لم يشهدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gradual growth in civilization concerns acquired theoretical knowledge, whereas awareness of needing a Lord is innate and foundational, so it does not arise later than other knowledge.
rows.anchor: وأما حديث تكامل الإنسان في العلم والحضارة تدريجا فإنما هو في العلوم النظرية الاكتسابية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses mean that God distinguished every descendant, made each testify to their own dependence, and took the covenant of His lordship so humanity cannot plead ignorance or inherited shirk.
rows.anchor: فالمتحصل من الآيتين أن الله سبحانه فصل بين بني آدم بأخذ بعضهم من بعض ثم أشهدهم جميعا على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: عدة من المفسرين
rows.claim: Several commentators take the time-setting as worldly life: God brings descendants through birth, displays His signs and their total dependence, and they acknowledge Him by the testimony of their state.
rows.anchor: ذكر عدة من المفسرين أن المراد بهذا الظرف المشار إليه

rows.speaker: القوم
rows.claim: A number of reports are cited for a primordial world of particles in which God extracted Adam's descendants, made them recognize Him, and took their covenant of lordship as proof for Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقد طرح القوم عدة من الروايات تدل على أن الآيتين تدلان على عالم الذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first objection says that if the extracted descendants were not rational they could not understand God's address, but if rational they should remember the covenant for it to establish proof; people recall no existence before earthly life.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يخلو إما أن جعل الله هذه الذرية المستخرجة من صلب آدم عقلاء أو لم يجعلهم كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second objection deems it implausible that a vast multitude forgot a known event when the Qur'an depicts people in Paradise and Hell recalling worldly events; it says this could otherwise permit the transmigrationists' account of repeated bodies.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يجوز أن ينسي الجميع الكثير والجم الغفير من العقلاء أمرا قد كانوا عرفوه وميزوه حتى لا يذكره ولا واحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third objection argues that the wording speaks of descendants from the backs of Adam's children, and the polytheist-ancestor excuse excludes Adam's immediate offspring from the primordial scene.
rows.anchor: 3 - ما أورد على الأخبار الناطقة بأن الله سبحانه أخذ من صلب آدم ذريته وأخذ منهم الميثاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict the verse to descendants with polytheist ancestors, excluding Adam's immediate children, believers, and polytheists without an idolatrous forebear.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم إن الآية خاصة ببعض بني آدم غير عامة لجميعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth objection says a single collective existence in the primordial world would leave no parents whose earlier polytheism descendants could cite.
rows.anchor: 4 - أن تفسير الآية بعالم الذر ينافي قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fifth view accepts the primordial reports as a pre-birth event that fosters an innate disposition toward knowledge of God, but argues the verse itself cannot mean that because descendants could plead that God made them forget the witness and left them to fallible reasoning.
rows.anchor: أن الروايات مقبولة مسلمة غير أنها ليست بتأويل للآية، والذي تقصه من حديث عالم الذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sixth objection says the verse is not explicit and could be figurative, while the reports are either raised or stopped traditions and carry no probative force.
rows.anchor: أن الآية لا صراحة لها فيما تدل عليه الروايات لإمكان حملها على التمثيل

rows.speaker: المثبتون لنشأة الذر
rows.claim: Defenders answer that forgetting the occasion and details of the covenant does not invalidate proof; the essential pledge and knowledge of God's oneness remain even if the scene is forgotten.
rows.anchor: فالجواب عن الأول أن نسيان الموقف وخصوصياته لا يضر بتمام الحجة وإنما المضر نسيان أصل الميثاق

rows.speaker: المثبتون لنشأة الذر
rows.claim: They answer that the alleged impossibility of mass forgetting is only an unsupported intuition; essential knowledge of lordship remains, and transmigration has separate refutations, so forgetting a prior world is not logically impossible.
rows.anchor: والجواب عن الثاني أن الامتناع من تجويز نسيان الجمع الكثير لذلك مجرد استبعاد من غير دليل على الامتناع
